history.claim: The Takua Pa Town Municipality's environmental operation plan document states that the Shrine in the Garden is named Seng Leng Keng Shrine and is hundreds of years old, without specifying the exact founding year.
history.quote: shrine that is hundreds of years old

history.claim: The municipality identified the founder as Mr. So Thian Seng, an overseas Chinese.
When the shrine was completed, the founder invited Phra Cheng Chui Cho Sue, or the Dewdrop God, which was brought from China, to be enshrined here.
The municipality document records the shrine's reputation regarding traditional Chinese healing. This is a history of beliefs and the role of the place, not evidence of treatment effectiveness.

A book stating the name of the Takua Pa Subdistrict Cultural Council mentions that Mr. So Seng was in the group of workers at Kue Chai Tung Shrine before opening the Shrine in the Garden. It is not verified if this name is the same person as Mr. So Thian Seng in the municipality document.

timeline.title: Founding of the shrine
timeline.detail: The municipality document identified the founder as Mr. So Thian Seng, an overseas Chinese, but did not specify the founding year.

timeline.title: Inviting the deity from China
timeline.detail: After building the shrine, Phra Cheng Chui Cho Sue, or the Dewdrop God, was invited from China to be enshrined.

timeline.title: Kosui snack activity in the Vegetarian Festival
timeline.detail: A review article reported the selling of Kosui snacks at the Shrine in the Garden, but it is not an official announcement and it is not verified if it will be held every year.

visit.best_time: The Vegetarian Festival is the period when there are reports of Kosui snacks being sold at the Shrine in the Garden, but no schedule for the shrine has been found for the current year.
